source.recordings: Crypton Drumbase 5000, Internet Archive drumbase-5k.7z, Partition D

measure: RMS log band-power error in dB over 43 ms overlapping windows, per-loop level matched and weighted by reference energy. Clean windows contain fewer than three near-full-scale source samples.

joint_gain_refinement.stage: Gain fit before the ring-down refinement

ringdown_refinement.method: Damped sinusoid fit to the early free ringing of unclipped or isolated hits. The fitted decay is the amplitude time constant. It differs from Roland's service calibration trace duration.

transient_and_fill_refinement.method: Fit the individual hit envelopes and pitch to both packs, then check the changes in the normal C groove renderer. The two high-bongo modes share a frequency. The snare adds a slower attack recovery with opposite polarity.

slow_rock_b_fill.measure: 40–135 Hz RMS measured 40–110 ms after the extra kick, as a ratio to nearby full kicks.
slow_rock_b_fill.drumbase_clipping_note: Some full-strength kick onsets clip. The clean-window groove metric rises from 3.19 to 3.68 dB.

isolated_waveform_check.measure: Waveform correlation in the 35–540 Hz band after independent gain, polarity and short lag matching.
isolated_waveform_check.note: The loop metric favors the new transient despite the weaker isolated-waveform match.

capture_balance_check.method: Fit the shunt model's steady-state Balance using the original mix-fit loops. Earlier refinements used the linear model at its historical fitted position.
capture_balance_check.scale: -1 is bass, 0 is center, +1 is treble.
capture_balance_check.recorded_knob_position: Unknown. The fitted control can also account for capture-chain differences.

noise_pulse_refinement.method: Measure short transients at cymbal-only and hi-hat-only steps, using nearby repeats to separate the coherent pulse from the noise. Add two decays of opposite sign to each voice. Compare the same C build at fixed Balance.

habanera_snare_check.method: Compare the documented Habanera A score to a temporary C build omitting the snare whenever the kick fires. Keep the documented score.
habanera_snare_check.build: Comparison made before the noise envelope refinement.

noise_envelope_refinement.method: Measure noise power on unclipped single-voice steps with at least 40 ms before the next hit. Fit a gate with a rising attack and an exponential discharge, then compare the full loops.

short_hat.selection_note: The measured hi-hat tails on Mambo and Cha-Cha are shorter than in Bossa Nova and Samba in both packs. Applying the short envelope globally increased the held-out groove error.

cymbal_refinement.method: Compare noise bands on 46 Drumbase and 67 Reverb cymbal hits away from other noise voices, excluding clipped windows. The same recordings inform the filter fit and the loop evaluation.
cymbal_refinement.kick_trial: A third decay reduced the 3–1000 Hz waveform error in both separated hits. It increased the first 45 ms waveform error with a 25–1000 Hz analysis band, so the production patch retains the earlier kick.
cymbal_refinement.build: Comparison before the fast hold and shared trigger change.

cymbal_gate_refinement.method: Compare hi-hat plus cymbal with hi-hat alone in the same clip, using 6.2–11.8 kHz power and excluding clipped windows. Compare cymbal-only tails in the previously measured loop windows.

latin_percussion_refinement.method: Level-matched reference/model traces from the rhythm captures at the same fixed Balance per pack as the previous pass. Measurements use selected hits without nearby competing onsets and exclude clipped windows.

low_bongo_fit.method: Damped sinusoid fitted over 10–78 ms of low-bongo bandpass (348–464 Hz) traces.

synthesis.rhumba_maracas: Short gate already used by Mambo and Cha-Cha.

cymbal_history_refinement.method: Estimate the first time the 6.1–11.6 kHz envelope falls 18 dB below the 8–24 ms attack. Use 10 ms windows and account for residual pre-hit noise. Compare hits with known cymbal history, no competing attacks during the measured span, and measurable cutoff in both renders.

settled_loop_comparison.method: Play one or two full Arrange cycles before matching a continuously playing hardware capture. Use the same fixed Balance settings and warm-up length for both C builds. Main report rows continue to use C from reset, preserving the earlier score methodology.

coincident_gate_refinement.method: In each recording, compare 6.2–11.8 kHz power of simultaneous hi-hat and cymbal triggers to the early power of single hi-hat triggers, using usable windows free of clipped samples and subsequent attacks. Compare the medians across the matched recordings. The settled loop check plays one or two complete Arrange cycles before scoring at the fixed per-pack Balance positions.

snare_gate_refinement.method: Align snare-only hits from the complete loops with the isolated one-shot from each pack, using the low-band waveform. Exclude windows close to another hit or containing PCM clipping. Measure noise in 1.3–14.5 kHz against its mean power across the 6–12, 12–23 and 23–40 ms windows. Compare this broadband level to the 235–360 Hz ring from 5–25 ms. Settled loop renders play one Arrange cycle before scoring.

provenance.note: The Vintage Synth Explorer demo and the matching archive hits count as one source.

arrange_timing_refinement.method: Transcribe both variation banks' pulses from figures 14 and 18, compare all three Arrange modes at 120 BPM against the actual host C event trace. For Jazz Waltz, compare figure 16 to a four-bar Auto capture from Drumbase. The downbeat comparison measures 235–355 Hz relative to 48–100 Hz at 5–34 ms.

wood_resonator_refinement.source: Roland TR-66 Service Notes, figures 10 and 19
wood_resonator_refinement.method: Fit a damped sinusoid to separated hits after the attack. Compare C renders before and after at fixed Balance after one Arrange cycle.

waltz_fill_refinement.source: Roland TR-66 Service Notes, figure 16, and Drumbase 66 WALTZ.wav
waltz_fill_refinement.method: Jointly fit damped sinusoids to the 43–93 Hz kick ring, 24–105 ms after each hit. Fit relative amplitudes against the median downbeat and exclude PCM-limited samples. Test the trigger levels in the complete C render.
waltz_fill_refinement.validation_note: Reverb Loop13.wav is Waltz A. The Drumbase recording is the only tested source with the fill.

hat_noise_filter_refinement.method: Compare the median short-time power in 12 bands, normalized to the 7.95–8.4 kHz band. Use the 6–26 ms window of hi-hat or maracas steps without coincident snare, cymbal, clipped samples or a following attack in the window.
hat_noise_filter_refinement.filter_note: Broaden and lower the first noise filter resonance. Adjust the existing two filter gains for approximately equal integrated noise power.

conga_attack_refinement.method: Align unclipped high conga hits by the 5–25 ms tonal ring and filter below 1.25 kHz to reduce maracas. Compare the first trough's magnitude with the first crest. Use fixed alignment and match ring level for both builds.

host_benchmark.selection: Mambo plus Rock 6, Arrange B, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

low_bongo_decay_refinement.isolated_hit_method: Low-pass the separated Beguine hits and C renders at 1.2 kHz. Normalize the Hilbert amplitude envelope to its mean from 6 to 16 ms.

host_benchmark.selection: Mambo plus Rock 6, Arrange B, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

hat_attack_refinement.method: Use unclipped hat or maracas steps without a simultaneous snare or cymbal. Band-pass each aligned recording and render, then divide each window's noise energy by the mean energy from 8 to 30 ms. Both packs were used to evaluate the candidate settings.

host_benchmark.selection: Mambo, Arrange A, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

balance_shunt_refinement.circuit_reference: Roland TR-66 Service Notes, Figures 1 and 10
balance_shunt_refinement.fit_scope: Independently refit one control position per capture pack on the original mix-fit subset. The objective uses settled C stems. Metrics below come from the PCM renderer.

host_benchmark.selection: Mambo, Arrange A, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

balance_shunt_refinement.limitation: The recordings contain no documented knob sweeps. The model represents gain at the dominant frequencies, and it needs a hardware sweep to verify frequency-dependent loading.

snare_pulse_refinement.scope: Fit the two pulse decays and the two ringing modes jointly to clean isolated hits. Regularize for the shape of the recorded attack. Evaluate coincident hits separately.

held_out_attack_measure.waveform_method: Peak normalized agreement, either polarity, with up to 3 ms alignment offset. Bandpass 72–700 Hz, first 50 ms.

host_benchmark.selection: Habanera, Arrange A, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

snare_pulse_refinement.limitation: The 110–240 Hz cancellation in coincident kick and snare hits remains stronger in the recordings. Drumbase isolated attack agreement decreases slightly.

bass_drum_pulse_refinement.scope: Bass drum ring and attack. Fit a shared continuous-start response to phase-aligned hits with only cymbal or hi-hat accompaniment. Give each capture equal weight within its pack.
bass_drum_pulse_refinement.attack_measure: Bandpass full aligned captures with third-order zero-phase Butterworth filters. Normalize correlation in 37–700 Hz from −4 to +61 ms with one gain and one lag of up to 5 ms per hit. Compute energy ratios on the fixed step grid, relative to the kick band for hits without snare and the snare ring for chords.
bass_drum_pulse_refinement.loop_measure: Same full C renderer and reference alignment as the preceding comparison. Settled runs play one Arrange cycle before the comparison interval.

host_benchmark.selection: Habanera, Arrange A, 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 64-frame blocks

bass_drum_pulse_refinement.limitation: The hardware has stronger 195–240 Hz cancellation on the kick and snare chords. The revised patch preserves common trigger timing. Differences in machine trims, recording gain, and voice interaction remain unresolved.

kick_snare_pair_drive.scope: Attenuate the tonal excitation to 85% when the only triggers are full kick and snare. Keep the snare noise gate at full drive.
kick_snare_pair_drive.training: Rock 5 in both packs. Reverb Habanera A is a held-out comparison against isolated snare hits. Cymbal combinations serve as controls.
kick_snare_pair_drive.measure: Reject clipped hits and require at least 187 ms since the preceding kick, 90 ms since the preceding snare, and 72 ms to the next event. Fit damped sinusoids for kick, snare and the higher snare resonance from 23–66 ms. Compare the magnitudes of the main rings within each recording.
kick_snare_pair_drive.host_benchmark: Median of nine paired passes. Habanera A at 200 BPM, 48 kHz, 200000 blocks per pass.
kick_snare_pair_drive.limitation: The level change does not reproduce the stronger cancellation in the original around 195–240 Hz. The drive fit establishes an output difference without identifying the circuit mechanism.

isolated_hit_reference.method: Measure 530–680 Hz power in 4–14, 14–32, 32–60 and 60–103 ms windows, relative to the first window. Compare median envelope levels and report mean absolute error across the four windows.

high_bongo_envelope_refinement.groove_error_measure: Level-matched weighted RMS log-band error in 43 ms windows.
